correctness.rationale: The published block formula (arXiv:2609.12569v1, Theorem 1 and Corollaries) matches the exact definition and initial values. The proof derives a single distinct reset ratio modulo every integer coprime to six, forcing memory-length divisibility of every tail period and a multiplicative-order condition. For k=2, parity forces even periods when the residual modulus is even. Exact 2-adic and 3-adic valuations give sharp last failing indices and hence exact first periodic indices by CRT. The independent direct-recurrence checker tests 2235 (k,M) pairs, excluding every proper divisor period and checking earliest index. Infinite conclusions rest on the argument, not the finite diagnostic.

value.rationale: The motivating primary paper explicitly asks for modular periodicity. For every memory length and every modulus, the finding determines two natural exact arithmetic invariants: least eventual period and least preperiod. It distinguishes persistent k=2 even-modulus behavior from the nilpotent 2/3 components at higher memory lengths, and gives a sharp formula for the first periodic index. Complete all-moduli classification is substantially more informative than a routine particular-prime congruence, while its dependence on the published scalar collapse is acknowledged.
